title: Non-defining Relative Clauses: Adding Insightful Commentary & Context
group: B1.3 - Critical Perspectives & Bridge to B2
objective: Menggunakan anak kalimat relatif non-defining dengan koma untuk memperkaya deskripsi tulisan dan tuturan lisan.

theory.summary: Non-defining relative clauses adalah anak kalimat relatif yang memberikan informasi tambahan (bonus) tentang noun yang sudah jelas identitasnya. Informasi ini bersifat extra commentary dan tidak esensial untuk memahami kalimat utama. Ciri khasnya: selalu dipisahkan dengan koma di awal dan akhir, dan TIDAK BOLEH menggunakan 'that'. Clause ini memperkaya deskripsi Anda dan membuat tulisan atau tuturan terdengar lebih sophisticated dan natural, cocok untuk level B1 yang mulai berkembang ke B2.
rules: Gunakan koma sebelum dan sesudah clause: Subject, who/which/whose + verb..., main verb. Contoh: My brother, who lives in Singapore, visits us twice a year.
Jangan gunakan 'that' dalam non-defining clauses. Gunakan 'who' untuk orang, 'which' untuk benda/hewan, 'whose' untuk kepemilikan. Contoh: The laptop, which I bought last month, works perfectly.

Informasi dalam clause bisa dihilangkan tanpa mengubah makna inti kalimat. Contoh: Dr. Sarah, who graduated from Oxford, is our new lecturer. (Tanpa clause: Dr. Sarah is our new lecturer - masih jelas siapa yang dimaksud).
Dalam bahasa lisan, tandai dengan jeda pendek atau intonasi menurun saat membaca clause ini. Contoh tertulis: The meeting, which lasted three hours, was very productive.

commonTrap.explanation: Siswa B1 sering lupa bahwa non-defining clauses WAJIB menggunakan koma dan TIDAK BOLEH memakai 'that'. Mereka juga kadang bingung kapan informasi itu esensial (defining) atau hanya tambahan (non-defining). Jika noun-nya sudah jelas tanpa perlu clause untuk mengidentifikasinya, gunakan non-defining dengan koma.
commonTrap.wrong: My supervisor that has worked here for twenty years is retiring next month.
commonTrap.correct: My supervisor, who has worked here for twenty years, is retiring next month.

vocab.collocation: My supervisor, who has excellent leadership skills, always supports our team.
Her expertise, which she gained through years of practice, is highly valued.
The company's headquarters, which are located in London, employ over 500 people.
The new software, which was developed in Germany, increases efficiency significantly.
My colleague, who joined the team last year, has already made a great impact.
The documentary, which won several awards, explores climate change issues.
Her manuscript, which took three years to complete, will be published next month.
The renovation, which cost thousands of pounds, has transformed the building.
His portfolio, which includes work from five countries, demonstrates his versatility.
The negotiations, which lasted several weeks, finally resulted in an agreement.

dialogue.context: Emma dan Daniel sedang membicarakan rekan kerja baru mereka dan proyek kantor yang sedang berjalan.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Have you met Rebecca, who joined our department last Monday?
lines.translation: Sudahkah kamu bertemu Rebecca, yang bergabung dengan departemen kita Senin lalu?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Yes! She's the one from the Manchester office, which recently won the innovation award, right?
lines.translation: Ya! Dia yang dari kantor Manchester, yang baru-baru ini memenangkan penghargaan inovasi, kan?

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Exactly. Her previous project, which involved AI technology, was really impressive.
lines.translation: Tepat sekali. Proyek sebelumnya, yang melibatkan teknologi AI, sangat mengesankan.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: I heard she'll be leading the marketing campaign, which starts next quarter.
lines.translation: Saya dengar dia akan memimpin kampanye pemasaran, yang dimulai kuartal depan.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: That's right. She's working with Tom, whose expertise in digital marketing is well-known.
lines.translation: Benar. Dia bekerja dengan Tom, yang keahliannya dalam pemasaran digital sudah terkenal.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Great! The new strategy, which focuses on social media, should bring excellent results.
lines.translation: Bagus! Strategi baru, yang fokus pada media sosial, seharusnya membawa hasil yang sangat baik.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: I'm optimistic too. Our CEO, who announced the plan yesterday, seems very confident.
lines.translation: Saya juga optimis. CEO kita, yang mengumumkan rencana itu kemarin, tampak sangat yakin.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: By the way, the office renovation, which was completed last week, looks amazing!
lines.translation: Omong-omong, renovasi kantor, yang selesai minggu lalu, terlihat luar biasa!

speakingLab.context: Anda sedang berbincang dengan Mr. Khoirul tentang orang-orang penting dalam hidup Anda dan tempat-tempat yang Anda kunjungi. Gunakan non-defining relative clauses untuk menambahkan informasi ekstra.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Hello! Today we'll practice adding extra information using non-defining clauses. Can you tell me about someone important in your life?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: My sister, who lives in Jakarta, is a doctor.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Excellent! You used the commas perfectly. How long has she been working as a doctor?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: She's been working for five years at a hospital, which is located in the city centre.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Well done! Now, tell me about a place you've visited recently. Remember to add extra commentary.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I visited Bali last month, which is famous for its beautiful beaches and temples.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Perfect use of non-defining clause! Can you describe someone you met there?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I met a tour guide, whose knowledge about Balinese culture was incredible, and he showed us many hidden places.

quiz.question: My manager, ___ has worked here for fifteen years, is very supportive.
quiz.explanation: Gunakan 'who' untuk orang dalam non-defining relative clauses. 'That' TIDAK BOLEH digunakan dalam non-defining clauses. Koma menunjukkan ini adalah non-defining clause yang memberikan informasi tambahan tentang 'my manager'.

quiz.question: The new office building, ___ was designed by a famous architect, opens next month.
quiz.explanation: Gunakan 'which' untuk benda (office building) dalam non-defining relative clauses. Koma di awal dan akhir clause menandakan ini adalah informasi tambahan yang tidak esensial. 'That' tidak boleh digunakan dalam non-defining clauses.

quiz.question: Dr. Williams ___ research focuses on climate change, will speak at the conference.
quiz.explanation: Koma WAJIB ada sebelum 'whose' karena ini non-defining clause. 'Whose' menunjukkan kepemilikan (research milik Dr. Williams). Tanpa koma, makna kalimat berubah dan menjadi defining clause.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly uses a non-defining relative clause?
options: My laptop that I bought last year is very fast.
My laptop, which I bought last year, is very fast.
My laptop, that I bought last year, is very fast.
quiz.answer: My laptop, which I bought last year, is very fast.
quiz.explanation: Opsi kedua benar karena menggunakan koma di awal dan akhir clause, serta menggunakan 'which' (bukan 'that'). Opsi pertama adalah defining clause tanpa koma. Opsi ketiga salah karena menggunakan 'that' dalam non-defining clause.

quiz.question: The documentary ___ won three awards ___ explores ocean pollution.
quiz.explanation: Koma diperlukan di KEDUA sisi non-defining clause (sebelum 'which' dan setelah 'awards'). Ini menandakan informasi tentang awards adalah tambahan. 'Which' adalah pilihan tepat untuk benda, dan 'that' tidak boleh digunakan dalam non-defining clauses.
